relearning.title: Read: unit conversions and scientific notation
relearning.description: A short reading with the money-trading analogy, worked examples and quick checks.

body.text:
**I can convert numbers into different units (dimensional analysis) and use scientific notation.**

**Think of trading money.** Four quarters and one dollar are the same amount of money, counted in different units. To trade 8 quarters for dollars, you use 4 quarters = 1 dollar and get 2 dollars. You didn't gain or lose money; only the unit changed. Converting units works the same way.

**Unit Relationships and conversion factors.** A **Unit Relationship** says how much of one unit equals another, like 1 ft = 12 in. Use the reference sheet; you don't have to memorize them. A **conversion factor** is the Unit Relationship written as a fraction, like 12 in / 1 ft. The top and bottom are the same amount, so a conversion factor is **equal to one**: it changes the units, not the amount.

**The 5 steps.** 1) **Identify**: given units on the left, wanted units on the right. 2) **Conversion Factors**: find the Unit Relationship. 3) **Set Up**: insert factors so the units cancel. Top vs Bottom: a unit on top cancels the same unit on the bottom. 4) **Calculate**: multiply the tops and divide by the bottoms. 5) **Sig Figs and Label**: no naked numbers!

**Worked example:** Convert 3.40 lb to kg. Unit Relationship: 1 kg = 2.205 lb. Set Up: 3.40 lb × (1 kg / 2.205 lb). The lb cancels: it is on top in 3.40 lb and on the bottom of the factor. Calculate: 3.40 ÷ 2.205 = 1.542. 3.40 has 3 sig figs, so the answer is **1.54 kg**.

checks.prompt: Which setup converts 15.0 kg to lb? (1 kg = 2.205 lb)
checks.explanation: kg is on top in 15.0 kg, so kg goes on the bottom of the factor to cancel: 2.205 lb / 1 kg. Flipping the factor so kg is on top is the common mistake, and 1 lb = 2.205 kg is not a real Unit Relationship.

checks.prompt: A student is 5.5 ft tall. How many inches is that? (1 ft = 12 in) Type a number.
checks.explanation: 5.5 ft × (12 in / 1 ft) = 66 in. Feet are on the bottom of the factor, so they cancel. Dividing by 12 (about 0.46) is the common mistake.

sections.title: Chains and scientific notation

body.text:
**Chains.** When there is no direct Unit Relationship, plan a path and use more than one factor. Every unit you don't want must cancel. Lined up, the factors look like a picket fence.

**Worked example 2:** Convert 1.50 ft to cm. Path: ft → in → cm. Set Up: 1.50 ft × (12 in / 1 ft) × (2.54 cm / 1 in). Feet cancel, then inches cancel. Calculate: 1.50 × 12 × 2.54 = 45.72. 1.50 has 3 sig figs, so the answer is **45.7 cm**. Exact numbers like 12 in = 1 ft have infinite sig figs, so they never limit your answer.

**Scientific notation** is digits with a decimal point after the first digit, times 10 to a power. The exponent is **positive** if you started with a big number (bigger than 1) and **negative** if you started with a small number (less than 1). Keep the same sig figs: 101,000 = 1.01 × 10^{5}.

**Worked example 3:** Write 0.000752 in scientific notation. Move the decimal 4 places right to get 7.52. The starting number is small, so the exponent is negative: **7.52 × 10⁻⁴**. Going back, 6.1 × 10^{3} has a positive exponent, so move the decimal 3 places right: **6,100**.

**Watch out for:** flipping a conversion factor (if the unit you have is on top of the factor, it won't cancel), dividing when you should multiply, giving the exponent the wrong sign, writing 45 × 10^{6} instead of 4.5 × 10^{7} (only one digit goes before the decimal), and leaving off the unit.

checks.explanation: Move the decimal 3 places right to get 3.85. The number is less than 1, so the exponent is negative. A positive exponent is the common mistake, and 38.5 × 10^{-4} has two digits before the decimal, so it isn't scientific notation.

checks.prompt: Convert 3.0 gal to cups. (1 gal = 4 qt, 1 qt = 4 cups) Type a number.
checks.explanation: 3.0 gal × (4 qt / 1 gal) × (4 cups / 1 qt) = 48 cups. Gallons cancel, then quarts cancel. Stopping after the first factor (12 qt) is the common mistake.

relearning.title: Do: convert step by step
relearning.description: Two worked conversions, one step at a time, with quick checks along the way.

body.problem: A dog has a mass of 22.7 kg. What is its mass in pounds (lb)? (1 kg = 2.205 lb)

steps.text: Identify. Given: 22.7 kg on the left. Wanted: lb on the right.
Conversion Factor. The Unit Relationship is 1 kg = 2.205 lb. It can be written as 2.205 lb / 1 kg or as 1 kg / 2.205 lb.
Set Up. kg is on top in 22.7 kg, so pick the factor with kg on the bottom: 22.7 kg × (2.205 lb / 1 kg). The kg cancel.
Sig Figs and Label. 22.7 has 3 sig figs, so the answer is 50.1 lb.

checks.prompt: Your turn: to convert 450 g to kg (1 kg = 1,000 g), which factor goes in the setup?
checks.explanation: g is on top in 450 g, so g goes on the bottom of the factor: 1 kg / 1,000 g. Then the grams cancel, leaving kg. Using the factor with g on top is the common mistake, because then nothing cancels.

checks.prompt: Your turn: convert 12.0 in to cm (1 in = 2.54 cm). Use the right sig figs. Type a number.
checks.explanation: 12.0 in × (2.54 cm / 1 in) = 30.48, and 12.0 has 3 sig figs, so the answer is 30.5 cm. Dividing (12.0 ÷ 2.54 = 4.72) is the common mistake.

body.problem: A science fair project runs for 2.50 days. How many seconds is that? Write the answer in scientific notation. (1 day = 24 hr, 1 hr = 60 min, 1 min = 60 s)

steps.text: Identify and plan. Given: 2.50 days. Wanted: s. There is no day = s relationship, so plan a path: days → hr → min → s.
Set Up: 2.50 days × (24 hr / 1 day) × (60 min / 1 hr) × (60 s / 1 min). Days cancel, then hours, then minutes, leaving s.
Scientific notation: move the decimal 5 places left to get 2.16. The number is big (bigger than 1), so the exponent is positive: 2.16 × 10^{5} s. That keeps the 3 sig figs of 2.50.

checks.prompt: Your turn: which setup converts 3.0 mi to inches? (1 mi = 5,280 ft, 1 ft = 12 in)
checks.explanation: Each factor puts the unit you want to cancel on the bottom: first mi, then ft. In choice c, the second factor is flipped, so ft does not cancel. A flipped factor is the common mistake.

checks.prompt: Your turn: which shows 6,020,000 in scientific notation?
checks.explanation: Move the decimal 6 places left to get 6.02. The number is bigger than 1, so the exponent is positive. 60.2 × 10^{5} has the right value but two digits before the decimal, the common mistake.

relearning.title: U1.LT3 Watch: conversion factors and scientific notation

checks.prompt: Why doesn't multiplying by the conversion factor 100 cm / 1 m change the amount you have?

options.text: The top and bottom are the same amount, so the factor is equal to one
100 is a big number, so it makes the amount bigger
Conversion factors only change the number, not the unit

checks.explanation: 100 cm and 1 m are the same length, so the factor is equal to one. Multiplying by one changes the units, not the amount, like trading 4 quarters for 1 dollar.

checks.prompt: Which setup converts 36 in to ft? (1 ft = 12 in)
checks.explanation: The unit you have (in) goes on the bottom of the factor so it cancels with the in on top: 36 ÷ 12 = 3 ft. Putting in on top of the factor, so it won't cancel, is the common mistake.

sections.title: Scientific Notation: Explained

checks.explanation: Move the decimal 7 places left to get 4.5. The starting number is big (bigger than 1), so the exponent is positive: 4.5 × 10^{7}. 45 × 10^{6} has two digits before the decimal, the common mistake.

checks.prompt: Write 3.2 × 10^{-3} as a regular number. Type a number.
checks.explanation: The exponent is negative, so the number is small: move the decimal 3 places left to get 0.0032. Moving it right (3,200) is the common mistake.
